jobs.title: VP, Portfolio Manager, Quantitative Investment
jobs.description:
Application Deadline:

12/04/2026

Address:
100 King Street West

Job Family Group:

Customer Solutions

The Quantitative Investment team manages approximately $20B CAD of active equity strategies.  The team employs a hybrid fundamental-quantitative approach, investing based on fundamental principles and implementing through a rigorous quantitative process.  The team has both internal and external clients across multiple distribution channels and manages product spanning ETF, Mutual Fund, Pool Fund and Separate Managed Accounts etc.

The team is looking for a Senior Quantitative Portfolio Manager to join an existing high performing team.  This position will be highly integral in all aspects of the investment process, including research and portfolio management, as well as contribute to overall team strategy and business development efforts through growing and servicing both internal and external channels.  The role is based in Toronto.
Primary responsibilities include:

Investments
- Managing and executing a fundamentally driven, quantitatively implemented active equity investment process
- Managing quantitative portfolios with overall responsibility for positioning, trading decisions, investment performance, and internal and external client communications
- Performing quantitative and/or  fundamental analysis to understand and validate proposed trades, as well as portfolio exposures
- Generating investment insights to be tested and implemented in the areas of stock selection, portfolio construction, and risk management
- Working with fundamental research analysts within the firm to translate investment insights into a systematic, data-driven investment process
- Overseeing and executing quantitative research projects
- Identifying and implementing opportunities to improve the investment process
- Overseeing platform development including production, research, and attribution capabilities, as well as new data sources and new analytical techniques

Business development
- Represent our process to internal and external clients:  educate internal sales and client service teams, meet with existing and potential clients in the institutional and retail channels, and become a trusted thought partner with internal channels including Multi Asset and Wealth channels

Leadership and management
- Help drive the business direction and growth strategy for the Canadian business
- Represents the business to internal and external constituents, including product, sales, client service
- Develop and mentor junior members of the team

Education/experience:
- Minimum 10 years’ experience working in active quantitative equity
- Minimum 5 years’ experience working as a portfolio manager in active quantitative equity
- Experience with quantitative equity investment experience required
- Experience working with clients required
- Graduate degree in business (MBA), finance, economics, mathematics or similar field preferred
- CFA charterholder or CIM required

The ideal candidate has:
- Desire to work on a fundamentally driven, quantitative implemented active equity investment team
- Strong understanding of quantitative investing
- Portfolio management experience
- Leadership and management experience – the ability to drive a business forward, identify and execute on a growth plan, and potentially manage junior team members
- Strong teamwork and communication skills
- Strong attention to detail along with demonstrated technical skills
- Strong presentation skills, including the ability to articulate complicated investment concepts in a way that resonates with various audiences, including consultants, institutional clients, and retail channels
- Comfort with technology and programming, with coding experience in R, Python, Matlab, and/or SQL attractive but not required

$80,000.00 - $175,000.00

Salaried

jobs.title: Relationship Manager, Commercial banking (Special Accounts)
jobs.description:
Application Deadline:

10/11/2026

Address:
320 S Canal Street

Job Family Group:
Customer Shared Services

Delivers an exceptional customer experience for a defined portfolio of high risk borrowing accounts by applying expertise to reduce the Bank’s loss exposure and manage risks. Advises internal and external stakeholders on complex, high-risk credit risk transactions and mitigation strategies. Makes credit decisions/recommendations in accordance with sound credit-granting principles and in compliance with Bank Policy & Procedures. Works with stakeholders to deepen relationships and grow the overall profitability of the portfolio.
- Recommends alternatives to credit proposals e.g. restructuring of the application and/or use of special loan plans available.
- Contributes to the development and implementation of lending related policies and procedures.
- Acts as a trusted advisor to assigned business/group.
- Influences and negotiates to achieve business objectives; includes action plans with debtor and guarantors.
- Recommends and implements solutions based on analysis of issues and implications for the business.
- Assists in the development of strategic plans.
- Identifies emerging issues and trends to inform decision-making.
- Identifies business needs, designs/develops tools and training programs; may include delivery of training to audiences.
- Helps determine business priorities and best sequence for execution of business/group strategy.
- Conducts independent analysis and assessment to resolve strategic issues.
- Ensures alignment between stakeholders.
- Integrates information from multiple sources to enable more efficient processes, enhanced analysis and/or streamlined reporting.
- Employs systems (e.g. customized exception reports, tracking reports etc.) to manage information.
- Breaks down strategic problems, and analyses data and information to provide insights and recommendations.
- Builds change management plans of varying scope and type; leads or participates in a variety of change management activities including readiness assessments, planning, stakeholder management, execution, evaluation and sustainment of initiatives.
- Leads or participates in defining the communication plan designed to positively influence or change behaviour; develops tailored messaging; and identifies appropriate distribution channels.
- Provides technical expertise to other team members, acting as a go-to person for the team.
- Supports the manager by coordinating and managing workflow and exception requests; escalates any concerns.
- Provides input into the planning and implementation of operational programs.
- Monitors the financial and risk performance of account portfolio; performs financial and risk analysis of customer and account information to provide insights and recommendations on how to improve quality, liquidity and Bank’s security position.
- Documents decisions on credit transactions with rationale that can be understood and explained to customers.
- Identifies and advises on terms, conditions and collateral requirements for the transaction decision as well as alternative solutions.
- Keeps abreast of economic and market developments within the portfolio to inform decision making and credit risk policies.
- Maintains and enhances knowledge around lending issues, including loan structure, collateral, foreclosure, bankruptcy and the various regulations that directly impact the Bank.
- Provides credit risk coaching and advice to sales & service employees to increase awareness of risk, policy, and knowledge of structuring transactions.
- Supports the execution of strategic initiatives in collaboration with internal and external stakeholders.
- Builds effective relationships with internal/external stakeholders; includes legal and insolvency professionals and other consultants/advisors in the commercial business community.
- Gathers and formats data into regular and ad-hoc reports, and dashboards.
- Monitors and tracks performance and addresses any issues.
- Provides input into the planning and implementation of operational programs.
- Executes work to deliver timely, accurate, and efficient service.
- Focus is primarily on business/group within BMO; may have broader, enterprise-wide focus.
- Provides specialized consulting, analytical and technical support.
- Exercises judgment to identify, diagnose, and solve problems within given rules.
- Works independently and regularly handles non-routine situations.
- Broader work or accountabilities may be assigned as needed.
- Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

Qualifications:
- Typically between 5 - 7 years of relevant experience and post-secondary degree in related field of study or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
- Credit Qualifications and associated credit knowledge and skills according to the established qualification standards.
- In-depth knowledge of banking products & services.
- In-depth knowledge of industry trends and regulations.
- In-depth knowledge of credit portfolio management policies & procedures, and financing guidelines.
- Proven leadership skills and highly developed coaching skills.
- Deep knowledge and technical proficiency gained through extensive education and business experience.
- Verbal & written communication skills - In-depth.
- Collaboration & team skills - In-depth.
- Analytical and problem solving skills - In-depth.
- Influence skills - In-depth.
- Data driven decision making - In-depth.

jobs.title: Analyst, Corporate Banking, Project and Energy Transition Finance
jobs.description:
Application Deadline:

10/10/2026

Address:
151 W 42nd Street

Job Family Group:
Capital Mrkts Sales & Service

Job Description

Supports the origination and structuring of project finance and structured lending transactions across a variety of industries and asset classes including power generation, utilities, infrastructure, energy and energy transition, and digital infrastructure. The individual will ultimately be responsible for supporting senior professionals in business development and day-to-day execution of these transactions. The position requires an individual who thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment and the ability to work independently with minimal guidance under time constraints will be a key differentiator of success.

Origination and Execution:
- Understand the construction, operational, and financing inputs to the project financial model including investing significant time in preparing and explaining credit scenarios and sensitivities, key metrics, and summary outputs

- Support, and eventually lead, various aspects of project financing transactions through to closing. These include but are not limited to:
- Credit analysis

- Risk and return analysis

- Due diligence (contracts, legal memoranda, etc.)

- Third-party consultant reports (independent engineer, market/insurance/environmental consultant, etc.)

- Credit documentation support (financing agreements, term sheets, etc.)

- Financial closing coordination

- AML/KYC and client onboarding activities and coordination

- Virtual data room (VDR) management

- Assist in preparing credit submissions (i.e., applications, memoranda, presentations, etc.) for internal (investment and risk committees) and external stakeholders (clients, investors, lenders, developers)

- Summarize diligence materials to develop and produce coherent recommendations and identify key risks and mitigants

- Run internal return models and capital committee memos

- Coordinate with credit and operations teams from origination through closing and funding

- Considers risk, internal controls and compliance as part of day-to-day accountabilities and adherence to policies and procedures

Qualifications:
- Undergraduate degree in business, finance/accounting, economics with outstanding academic achievement (academic transcript to be provided if available)

- Financial services experience analyzing large corporate, commercial or project finance credit risk

- Project finance experience is an asset, especially financial modelling experience and proficiency

- Strong organizational and time-management skills with exceptional attention to detail

- Outstanding communication (written, oral, listening) and interpersonal skills with ability to present complex information succinctly to internal and external audiences

- Self-starter with ability to learn quickly and work independently while also being able to work effectively in a team environment

- Desire and willingness to demonstrate accountability and proactively anticipate team needs

- Highly proficient in Excel, PowerPoint, Word

- Strong working knowledge of and ability to leverage AI to drive efficiency will be considered an asset

The salary range for this role is $95,000.00 up to $110,000.00 USD (subject to the candidate meeting the specific skills, experience, education, and qualification requirements)

jobs.title: Senior Manager, AI Strategy & Product Management
jobs.description:
Application Deadline:

11/08/2026

Address:
100 King Street West

Job Family Group:

Data Analytics & Reporting

Senior Manager – AI Strategy & Product Management

This role will shape BMO InvestorLine's AI portfolio and drive meaningful AI value creation for our clients and teams. The Senior Manager will combine strategy, product management, and transformation leadership to define AI priorities, translate opportunities into actionable roadmaps, lead AI products from discovery through launch and adoption, and ensure measurable value is realized within a responsible AI and regulatory framework.

The successful candidate will bring structured problem solving, strong business judgment, technical fluency in modern AI capabilities, and a proven ability to move from strategy through execution in a highly matrixed and regulated environment.

AI Strategy & Value Creation
- Own and evolve BMO InvestorLine's AI strategy, portfolio, and multi-year roadmap, aligning business objectives, client needs, market opportunities, enterprise priorities, and regulatory requirements.
- Identify, assess, and prioritize AI opportunities, balancing value, feasibility, risk, dependencies, and resource constraints to maximize client and business impact.
- Develop quantitative business cases, value measurement frameworks, investment recommendations, and executive decision materials to support portfolio governance and funding decisions.
- Build alignment across business, technology, data, design, operations, risk, compliance, legal, and external partners to accelerate delivery and responsible AI adoption.
- Advise senior leaders on AI trends, competitive developments, emerging technologies, and strategic implications through clear, data-driven recommendations.

AI Product Management
- Define product vision, strategy, roadmaps, and success measures for AI-powered client and employee experiences.
- Lead product discovery and prioritization by integrating client research, analytics, market intelligence, business objectives, and technical considerations into actionable product requirements.
- Lead E2E product delivery by partnering with technology, data, architecture, and design teams to translate strategic objectives into scalable, production-ready AI solutions.
- Lead vendor evaluations, partner engagements, and major product decisions, balancing client value, business outcomes, technical feasibility, operational readiness, and regulatory requirements.
- Guide products through the full lifecycle from concept and experimentation through launch, adoption, optimization, and value realization, leveraging analytics, experimentation frameworks, A/B testing, and client feedback to continuously improve outcomes.

Qualifications
- 6+ years of progressive experience spanning strategy and product, including a minimum of 2 years in management consulting and 2 years as a Product Manager or Product Owner for AI-powered products, platforms, or capabilities.
- Demonstrated experience developing AI strategies, business cases, and prioritized roadmaps, successfully translating them into delivered products, measurable adoption, and realized business value. You must have shipped an AI product to be considered for this role.
- Deep understanding of modern AI technologies, architectures, and delivery practices, including the AI software development lifecycle (AI SDLC), evaluation frameworks, guardrails, orchestration, observability, and multi-agent systems. This is not an AI engineering role , but requires sufficient technical fluency to shape strategy, define product requirements, make informed trade-offs, and drive execution.
- Proven ability to develop executive narratives, influence strategic decisions, and lead complex cross-functional initiatives across business, technology, data, design, operations, risk, legal, compliance, and external partners.
- Strong understanding of responsible AI, governance, privacy, security, and regulatory requirements, particularly within financial services or other highly regulated industries.
- Exceptional communication skills, executive presence, ownership, accountability, and comfort operating in ambiguous environments while balancing strategic thinking with hands-on execution.
- Previous experience in a highly regulated industry is strongly preferred.
- MBA/MSc/PhD is an asset.

jobs.title: Personal Banking Associate
jobs.description:
Application Deadline:

10/22/2026

Address:
435 Stone Road

Job Family Group:

Retail Banking Sales & Service

Delivers exceptional service to BMO customers and prospects. Identifies customer needs and provides advice and guidance regarding financial solutions that are in the best interests of customers. Works collaboratively within the branch and through various channels with BMO partners to deliver the desired customer experience and achieve overall business objectives.

- Collaborates with BMO partners to identify referral opportunities that further grow the customer’s relationship with BMO beyond personal banking.
- Welcomes and guides customers as they walk into the branch lobby, and offers advice and guidance on available digital and self-serve options with the goal of making it easy, simple, and fast to bank with BMO.
- As a lobby leader, assists in conducting client conversations about banking services to recommend alternative banking channels and  provide personal banking and investment advice.
- Meets customer transaction-based needs with seamless execution.
- Reviews customer profiles and engages customers in a needs-based conversation to identify potential opportunities and address everyday banking plans and credit card needs.
- Contributes to meeting branch business results and the customer experience.
- Supports operational activities (e.g. inventory management, escalated service requests, following up on customer applications, filing, opening and closing activities).
- Acts as a key member of a collaborative and versatile branch and market team.
- Probes to understand customer personal banking and credit card needs and integrates marketing promotions and programs into customer conversations to provide strategic advice.
- Organizes work information to ensure accuracy and completeness.
- Takes the initiative to find creative approaches that make each customer’s experience feel personal.
- Looks for ways to contribute to the ongoing improvement of the overall customer experience.
- Contributes to business results and the overall experience delivered.
- May work at multiple branches or through various channels based on market needs; work schedule may differ from week to week in terms of days worked, hours, and shifts.
- Follows through on risk and compliance processes and policies to ensure we safeguard our customers’ assets, maintain their privacy, and act in their best interest.
- Keeps current with the wider financial services marketplace, the legal and regulatory environment, and our commitment to uphold the highest ethical requirements of our industry.
- Maintains current knowledge of personal banking products, practices, and trends and integrates into customer conversations.
- Identifies and reports suspicious patterns of activity that are suspected to be related to money laundering.
- Complies with legal and regulatory requirements for the jurisdiction.
- Protects the Bank's assets in compliance with all regulatory, legal, and ethical requirements.
- Completes complex & diverse tasks within given rules/limits.
- Analyzes issues and determines next steps; escalates as required.
- Broader work or accountabilities may be assigned as needed.
- Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

Qualifications:
- Typically between 1 – 2 years of relevant experience and/or certification in related field of study desirable or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
- Canada only: Registration to sell investment products completed or in progress (must be completed within 12 months) - as appropriate for the jurisdiction.
- Confident and experienced in the use of social media, tablets, Smart phones, online tools, and applications.
- Some experience in a consultative customer service or sales roles, with a drive to deliver a personal customer experience.
- Basic knowledge of specialized sales and business banking solutions to refer to specialists.
- Passionate commitment to helping customers.
- Drive to deliver a personal customer experience.

jobs.description:

Business Overview
Treasury & Payment Solutions (TPS) is a strategic business within BMO's North American Integrated Solutions (NAIS) platform, delivering payment, treasury management, commercial card, merchant acquiring, liquidity, and cash management capabilities to commercial, corporate, institutional, and government clients across North America. As a critical enabler of client growth and the movement of money, TPS supports organizations through innovative payment solutions, operational excellence, and prudent risk management.

The TPS Governance & Controls team serves as the first line of defense risk and governance function for TPS and is responsible for ensuring that risk management practices keep pace with business growth, product innovation, regulatory expectations, and evolving operational risks. The team partners closely with business leaders, product teams, operations, compliance, legal, technology, and second line risk functions to identify, assess, monitor, and mitigate risk while enabling strategic business objectives.

The Opportunity
The Director, TPS Risk Advisory plays a key leadership role within TPS Governance & Controls, providing strategic risk oversight and trusted advisory support across a diverse portfolio of payment, treasury, and commercial banking products and services. The role is responsible for partnering with business executives and key stakeholders to assess new initiatives, product changes, emerging risks, regulatory developments, and operational challenges to ensure risks are appropriately identified, understood, and managed.

The successful candidate will lead a team of risk professionals responsible for providing governance and risk advisory coverage across TPS initiatives, programs, products, and client-facing activities. This includes oversight of risk assessments, issue management, audit and regulatory engagement support, control design and effectiveness reviews, change initiatives, third-party risk considerations, and the implementation of risk mitigation strategies.

As a member of the TPS Governance & Controls leadership team, this role contributes to the broader mandate of protecting the organization, strengthening the control environment, supporting sustainable business growth, and ensuring the ongoing safety, soundness, and resilience of BMO's Treasury & Payment Solutions business

- Fosters a culture aligned to BMO purpose, values and strategy and role models BMO values and behaviours in all that they do.

jobs.title: Senior Relationship Manager, Commercial Banking (Financial Services Group)
jobs.description:
Application Deadline:

10/18/2026

Address:
100 King Street West

Job Family Group:

Commercial Sales & Service

Global Team Overview:
The selected candidate will join the Financial Services Group, part of Advisory Solutions within BMO Commercial Bank, Canada. The Group focuses on management and origination of banking relationships within the Financial Services sector, with a focus on senior debt financing opportunities with Non-Bank Financial Institutions as well as full banking relationships with select Financial Services firms and FinTechs. It assesses financing opportunities representing $10MM or more, both on a syndicated and bilateral basis, for both private and public companies in Canada. The Group is based in Toronto and has national coverage in the sector.

Job Overview
The Director will join the Financial Services Group team and will be responsible for:
- Managing an established portfolio comprised of relationships with increasing credit needs and complex Treasury and Payment Solutions requirements. The Director will aim to grow such portfolio through significant business development and ongoing management of key client relationships.
- Grow revenue, deposits, and wallet share through proactive business development.
- Deepen relationships with clients that have complex Treasury & Payment Solutions requirements.
- Execute on and coordinate a national origination strategy in the sector, specifically for Money Services Businesses, FinTechs and select Virtual Currency businesses.
- Continue the development and establishment of a comprehensive analysis framework to assess and review current and prospective relationships key operational and reputational risks.
- Liaise with key stakeholders, SMEs and product partners to help develop and deliver customized products and services to key existing and prospective clients.
- Ensuring the required internal control standards, including adherence to audit, regulatory and compliance policies.

The selected candidate:

Makes recommendations to senior leaders on strategy and new initiatives, based on an in-depth understanding of the business/group.
- Develops the business case by identifying needs, analysing potential options and assessing expected return on investment.
- Advises on sales strategy based on a deep understanding of the market, relevant industry verticals, market competitors, client needs and business growth opportunities.
- Leads and executes business development plans to that business goals are achieved or exceeded.

Leads sales activities, including:
- Leads team in pre-sales activities such as pitch preparation, client research, preparation of prospect and client files for further action.

jobs.description:
Application Deadline:

11/20/2026

181 Bay Street

POSITION OVERVIEW
Organization: Burgundy Asset Management Ltd
Title: Investment Analyst
Reports to: Portfolio Manager of Fixed Income & Credit Strategies
Location: In person/on-site at 181 Bay Street, Suite 4510, Toronto, ON, M5J 2T3

POSITION SUMMARY
We are seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented Fixed Income & Credit Investment Analyst to join Burgundy’s investment team. The successful candidate will play a key role in identifying, analyzing, and monitoring high-quality investment opportunities consistent with the firm’s long-term investment philosophy.
This role is well suited for an intellectually curious, highly analytical individual who enjoys deep fundamental research and values independent thinking. The analyst will work closely with the Portfolio Manager and other members of the investment team and will have meaningful responsibility and visibility within the investment process.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
·         Conduct fundamental and quantitative research on fixed income securities – primarily investment grade and high yield corporate bonds but may also include government bonds, municipal debt, structured credit products, convertible bonds, preferred shares, and hybrid securities.
·         Monitor credit quality, interest rate movements, economic indicators, and sector or industry trends to evaluate investment risks and opportunities.
·         Develop and maintain financial models and analyze covenants and legal documentation to support investment decisions.
·         Prepare and deliver investment recommendations, market commentary, and research reports to portfolio managers, senior leadership and relationship managers.
·         Support portfolio construction and risk management processes, including duration analysis, yield curve positioning, and credit exposure assessment.
·         Track the performance of fixed income portfolios relative to benchmarks and identify key drivers of performance.
·         Stay up to date with regulatory developments, macroeconomic events, and market conditions that affect fixed income markets.
·         Collaborate with traders, portfolio managers, and other analysts; contribute to internal investment discussions and debates, bringing independent perspectives and thoughtful challenge.
·         Uphold Burgundy’s high standards for intellectual rigor and integrity.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR
·         4+ years of prior professional experience in investment research, preferably fixed income & credit, though equity research will also be considered.
·         Strong understanding of fixed income instruments, credit markets, and valuation methodologies.
·         Demonstrated passion for investing and a genuine interest in understanding businesses.
·         Intellectual curiosity and confidence to challenge consensus views with well-supported analysis.
·         Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, solid financial and business acumen, and meticulous attention to detail.
·         Effective written and verbal communication and presentation abilities, with the capacity to clearly articulate complex ideas.
·         Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment.
·         Sound judgment, integrity, and alignment with a long-term, owner-oriented investment mindset.

THE FIXED INCOME & CREDIT TEAM
The Fixed Income Team at Burgundy manages four distinct funds:
·         The Bond Fund – Established in May 1999, this fund focuses on government and investment grade bonds.
·         The Strategic Credit Fund – Launched in August 2005, this fund invests in both investment grade and high-yield bonds.
·         The Investment Grade Credit Fund – Created in January 2018, this fund is dedicated exclusively to investment grade bonds.
·         A dedicated High Yield Credit Fund – Specializes in high-yield bonds.

WHY BURGUNDY
·         Work in a high-conviction culture where rigorous analysis and independent thinking are central to the investment process.
·         Take ownership and have a real impact with research informing portfolio decisions.
·         Develop as an investor over the long term, with access to experienced professionals and a culture committed to mentorship, learning, and professional growth.
·         Engage with businesses and management teams directly, building a stronger understanding of what drives sustainable performance.
·         Competitive compensation and benefits package.
·         Opportunities for professional growth and advancement.

HIRING PROCESS TIMELINE

Your application package should include:
- Resume
- Cover Letter; included at the bottom of your cover letter, please answer the following question in 250 words or less (please do not use AI): What has been your biggest investment mistake, and what did you learn from it?

Interviews will be conducted in November and December 2026.

We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

ABOUT BURGUNDY ASSET MANAGEMENT LTD
Burgundy Asset Management Ltd is a global investment manager providing discretionary investment management for private clients and institutions. Founded in 1990, we invest with a long-term, fundamental approach – building concentrated portfolios of high-quality businesses to protect and compound clients’ capital over time. Our culture is grounded in honesty, courage, and doing what is right for our clients – and we look for candidates who share these values.
Burgundy Asset Management is a division of BMO Financial Group. Within BMO Wealth Management, Burgundy functions as an independent line of business.

jobs.description:
Application Deadline:

10/29/2026

Address:
100 King Street West

Job Family Group:

Commercial Sales & Service

Corporate Finance Team Overview:
The Corporate Finance team within Canadian Commercial Banking, is part of BMO Financial group and covers both public and large private corporate clients operating in diversified industries. The team is responsible for marketing, managing, and monitoring large commercial loan portfolios, and also supporting credit requirements and cross selling efforts for other businesses including subordinated debt, equipment leasing, derivatives, cash management, and trade finance. The team assesses financing opportunities of $10,000,000 or more, both on a syndicated and bilateral basis.

Job Overview
The Senior Relationship Manager manages a commercial lending portfolio and supports the origination of new clients, and coordinates with other products as an integral part of a larger coverage team that maintains strong client relationships.  Facilitates growth initiatives for the Bank through significant business development and excellent management of key client relationships by cross selling other products (e.g., derivatives, cash management & corporate cards, subordinated debt and equity, leasing, trade finance products, etc.).

We are currently hiring for multiple Sales Director roles across several Greater Toronto Area locations, including First Canadian Place (Toronto) or Vaughan Metropolitan Centre (Vaughan).

Facilitates growth for the Bank through business development and management of key client relationships. Maintains an outstanding and continuous record of significant revenue generation from sales and syndications.
- Acts as an escalation point for complex client issues, using strategic problem-solving to resolve conflicts and maintaining strong client relationships.
- Leads the structuring of high-value, complex deals, and credit approvals, ensuring alignment with client needs.
- Oversees credit approvals and drives pricing coordination, acting as the primary client advocate to ensure alignment with client needs and bank objectives.
- Drives negotiations for high-value, complex transactions and credit approvals, ensuring deals are structured to meet client needs.
- Manages high-value client portfolios, driving cross-selling, retention, and profitability.
- Implements cross-selling initiatives, driving client engagement and successfully transitioning opportunities into revenue-generating sales.
- Leads market coverage strategies to expand portfolios, identify opportunities, and align with business goals.
- Represents bank at industry forums and conferences, leveraging insights on trends, competition, and emerging products to drive strategic decision-making.
- Engages with senior leadership and cross-functional teams to align strategies, address client needs, and drive holistic business solutions.
- Delivers reports to the bank’s leadership on team performance, client satisfaction, market trends, and key strategic initiatives, delivering insights that inform corporate strategy.
- Drives strategic advisory on loan products, options, rates, terms, and collateral requirements, ensuring tailored solutions that align with client needs and business objectives.
- Builds and maintains strong long-term relationships with the bank’s high-value and strategic clients, providing strategic advice on financial solutions and ensuring exceptional service and partnership.
- Structures deals, secures credit approvals, negotiates high-value transactions, and identifies opportunities for cross-selling.
- Analyzes market trends, client industry developments, and competitive positioning to inform client solution strategies and optimize client satisfaction.
- Works closely with internal teams and stakeholders to define products, solutions and strategies that best fit clients’ needs.
- Identifies share of wallet opportunities.
- Leverages analysis tools to nurture and grow a portfolio that exceeds ROE thresholds and evaluates client returns on a proactive basis.
- Ensures adherence to regulatory requirements, internal controls, and compliance policies in all aspects of relationship management, mitigating risk and maintaining service standards.
- Operates at a group/enterprise-wide level and serves as a specialist resource to senior leaders and stakeholders.
- Applies expertise and thinks creatively to address unique or ambiguous situations and to find solutions to problems that can be complex and non-routine.
- Implements changes in response to shifting trends.
- Broader work or accountabilities may be assigned as needed.
- Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

Qualifications:
- 10+ years of relevant experience in Relationship Management, Account Management or Portfolio Management in a corporate or similar segmented banking environment with sales metrics is preferred.
- Bachelor’s degree required; Business Administration, Finance and Accounting preferred. Any other related discipline or commensurate work experience considered.
- If a Credit Qualifiable role, Credit Qualifications and associated credit knowledge and skills according to the credit portfolio requirements and qualification standards.
- Seasoned professional with a combination of education, experience and industry knowledge.

Advanced level of proficiency:
- Project Management
- Change Management

Expert level of proficiency:
- Product Knowledge
- Regulatory Compliance
- Structuring Deals
- Portfolio Management
- Credit Risk Assessment
- Customer Service
- Stakeholder Management
- Negotiation
- Customer Relationship Building

Salaried

BMO Capital Markets is a leading, full-service financial services provider. We offer corporate and investment banking, treasury management, as well as research and advisory services to clients around the world. #bmocapitalmarkets

Mandate
BMO Capital Markets is seeking a Vice President, Business Management, Global Fixed Income to support the continued growth and operational excellence of our Global Fixed Income (GFI) business.
This is a front-office role at the center of the franchise. Working directly with — and as the principal deputy to — the Managing Director, Strategy & Business Management, the Vice President will independently own a substantial portion of the GFI business management agenda: performance reporting and analysis, business planning, governance and control processes, cross-functional issue resolution, and execution of strategic initiatives. The role provides direct exposure to the Co-Heads of GFI and the broader GFI leadership team, including partnering with senior executives across Rates, Credit, FX, Securitized Products, Debt Capital Markets, Electronic Trading, and XVA.
The successful candidate will combine strong commercial acumen, exceptional organizational skills, sound judgment, and the ability to influence senior stakeholders across a highly matrixed global organization. The Vice President will be expected to take ambiguous problems, define the work, drive it to resolution, and escalate with facts, options, and a recommendation.

Key Responsibilities
Support the Co-Heads of Global Fixed Income
- Serve as a trusted strategic partner to the Co-Heads of GFI.
- Prepare executive briefing materials, talking points, communications, presentations, and business updates for internal and external stakeholders.
- Track commitments, decisions, and action items from senior leadership discussions and ensure timely follow-through.
- Anticipate issues, identify emerging risks, and proactively escalate matters requiring executive attention.
- Coordinate GFI leadership offsites, town halls, employee engagement activities, and executive communications.

Business Performance & Management Reporting
- Own the recurring GFI management reporting cycle, including daily and monthly P&L reporting, business review materials, monthly and quarterly commentary, and working with the Business Coordinator to populate and maintain KPIs and league tables.
- undefined

- undefined

- undefined
- Develop a working understanding of how the numbers are constructed. Investigate large period-over-period jumps and estimate vs. actual discrepancies in financials, identify and run to ground cost savings opportunities, expense misallocations, issues with P&L calculations, etc.

Business Execution & Operational Excellence
- Support strategic growth initiatives and new product launches across the GFI platform.
- Partner with Sales, Trading, Structuring, Technology, and Operations to translate front-office requirements into scalable technology and process improvements.
- Drive automation, controls enhancement, workflow optimization, and other initiatives that improve efficiency, reduce operational risk, and enhance the client experience.
- Own routine business infrastructure requests, including new portfolio and cost center set ups.
- Represent GFI Front Office in initiatives that span across businesses, including regulatory inquiries, risk management buildouts, new infrastructure.

Strategic Planning and Executive Governance
- Support the MD, Strategy & Business Management in shaping and executing the GFI strategic agenda, translating enterprise and business priorities into actionable plans and measurable outcomes.
- Conduct market, competitor, and industry analysis to identify opportunities, risks, and actions to improve business performance and client outcomes.
- Lead preparation of materials for executive committees, P&L walkthroughs, management committees, board reporting, regulatory reviews, and senior leadership meetings.
- Track key initiatives and franchise priorities, highlighting progress, dependencies, risks, and required decisions.

Stakeholder Management
- Build strong relationships across Front Office, Operations, Technology, Finance, Risk, Compliance, Legal, and Corporate Functions.
- Facilitate communication and issue resolution across regions and functional teams.
- Represent business priorities in cross-functional working groups, governance committees, and project forums.

Qualifications
Required
- 5-8+ years of experience in Global Markets, Investment & Corporate Banking or Management Consulting.
- Experience supporting senior executives and operating effectively within a complex global organization.
- Demonstrated ability to own workstreams end-to-end with limited supervision, and to operate effectively with competing priorities and incomplete information.
- Demonstrated success leading strategic initiatives and influencing stakeholders without direct authority.
- Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including preparation of executive and board-level materials.
- Strong analytical, financial, and problem-solving capabilities.
- Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and operate effectively under pressure.
- Advanced proficiency in PowerPoint and Excel. The candidate will need to be able to draft business plan pitch decks that tell a story as opposed to simply stating facts, and build excel models with limited information.

Preferred
- Working knowledge of fixed income products and the trade lifecycle across rates, credit, securitized products, or FX.
- Familiarity with front-office risk, P&L, and booking systems, and with regulatory and capital concepts relevant to a dealer business.
- SQL, Power BI, Power Query, or comparable data and automation skills.

Success Measures
The successful candidate will:
- Serve as a trusted advisor to the Co-Heads of Global Fixed Income and the MD, Strategy & Business Management, Global Fixed Income.
- Measurably increase the MD's capacity to focus on strategic priorities and the most complex escalations.
- Assume full ownership of the recurring GFI reporting and business management calendar, delivered accurately and on time with minimal MD involvement.
- Improve the efficiency and effectiveness of executive decision-making and governance.
- Exhibit curiosity in understanding the mechanics of operations, how metrics are calculated, and why processes are implemented the way they are
- Deliver high-quality insights and materials that support informed strategic decisions, including iterating quickly on materials to ensure quick feedback cycles.
- Drive execution of franchise priorities while strengthening alignment, accountability, operational discipline, and employee engagement across the leadership team.

The CIAM Operations Lead / SRE Lead is responsible for ensuring the reliability, availability, security, scalability, and operational excellence of Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) platforms. The role leads day-to-day operations, production support, automation initiatives, platform modernization efforts, and Site Reliability Engineering practices across critical identity services supporting customer authentication, authorization, MFA, SSO, consent management, and digital onboarding journeys.
This individual will be responsible for platform stability, incident management, observability, infrastructure lifecycle management, security compliance, and continuous service improvement while partnering closely with Development, Security, Infrastructure, Architecture, and Business stakeholders. Responsibilities align closely with CIAM Engineering & Operations activities such as infrastructure management, deployments, vulnerability remediation, monitoring, and 24x7 operational support.

Site Reliability & Service Ownership
- Own the operational health, availability, performance, and resilience of CIAM platforms.
- Define and maintain SLIs, SLOs, and error budgets for critical customer identity services.
- Drive adoption of SRE practices, reliability engineering standards, and operational excellence principles.
- Lead capacity planning, performance tuning, and resiliency testing.

- Eliminate manual operational activities through tooling and self-service capabilities.
- Define and maintain enterprise monitoring and observability standards.
- Develop proactive alerting, anomaly detection, dashboards, and operational reporting.
- Improve signal-to-noise ratio and reduce false-positive alerts.

Security & Compliance
- Ensure compliance with cybersecurity policies, regulatory requirements, and audit standards.
- Lead vulnerability remediation and platform currency initiatives.
- Oversee security controls for customer identity data and authentication services.
- Partner with Security and Risk teams during audits, assessments, and regulatory reviews.

Release & Change Management

- Ensure successful execution of maintenance windows and platform upgrades.
- Implement DevSecOps and CI/CD best practices.
- Review deployment readiness and post-implementation validation activities.

Leadership & Stakeholder Management

- Collaborate with Development, Architecture, Product, Security, and Infrastructure teams.
- Provide executive-level communication regarding service health, incidents, risks, and improvement initiatives.

Education
- University degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related discipline.
- Relevant industry certifications are considered an asset.

Experience
- 6+ years of experience supporting enterprise IAM/CIAM platforms.
- 3+ years of experience providing technical leadership for enterprise-scale platforms and complex engineering initiatives.
- Experience managing mission-critical customer-facing applications.
- Experience operating large-scale, highly available authentication and authorization platforms.

- CIAM/IAM technologies (ISVA, ISAM, or equivalent)
- OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SAML
- Linux and middleware administration
- WebSphere, LDAP
- Knowledge of AWS, Azure, or GCP cloud platforms.
- Strong knowledge of CI/CD pipelines, GitHub, Infrastructure as Code, and cloud-native technologies.
- Ansible, Terraform, Python, Shell scripting
- Hands-on experience with enterprise monitoring and observability platforms such as Dynatrace, Splunk, Grafana, and AppDynamics.
- Experience with AIOps tools, event management platforms, and intelligent automation solutions.

Success Metrics
The CIAM Operations Lead / SRE will be measured on:
- Platform reliability, resiliency, and operational stability.
- SLA/SLO attainment
- MTTR reduction
- Incident reduction and prevention
- Automation adoption and operational efficiency gains through AIOps capabilities.
- Team engagement and capability development
- Drive measurable contributions toward BMO's Ambition 2030 objectives through innovation, accountability, automation, and engineering excellence.

This role combines traditional Operations leadership with modern Site Reliability Engineering practices to deliver secure, resilient, highly available CIAM services that support critical digital banking and customer identity journeys.

- Oversee complex fraud investigations, ensuring threats are identified, assessed, escalated, and resolved in accordance with regulatory requirements, internal policies, and risk frameworks.

jobs.title: Associate, Global Markets Corporate Banking
jobs.description:
Application Deadline:

12/30/2026

Address:
100 King Street West

Job Family Group:

Capital Mrkts Sales & Service

BMO Capital Markets is a leading, full-service financial services provider. We offer corporate and investment banking, treasury management, as well as research and advisory services to clients around the world. #bmocapitalmarkets

The Associate will be part of the Global Markets Corporate Banking Securitization team, which is responsible for underwriting and account management of securitization and other structured finance transactions across a wide variety of asset classes, including, but not limited to, automobile loans and leases, equipment loans, student loans, credit cards, consumer installment loans, residential mortgage-backed securities, commercial mortgage-backed securities, and leveraged loans for U.S. and Canadian clients. The Associate will independently execute core credit underwriting and portfolio management activities, provide well-supported approval recommendations regarding transaction structures and exposure amounts, and serve as a key day-to-day partner to Account Managers, clients, Credit, and product partners. The Associate will also contribute to transaction execution, portfolio surveillance, risk management, and business initiatives, while providing guidance to Analysts as appropriate.
Credit Risk and Financial Analysis
- Prepare concise, accurate, and well-reasoned credit applications and memoranda for new and existing transactions, with limited supervision, for presentation to Credit.
- Lead credit risk analysis of securitization transactions using available sources of information, including servicer reports, cash flow models, financial statements, servicer audits, legal documentation, and third-party research.
- Develop and clearly articulate approval recommendations regarding transaction structure, exposure, risk rating, capital, and key mitigants.
- Determine estimated capital for current and prospective securitization transactions using the Bank’s applicable capital models and analyze the effect of structural alternatives.
- Conduct due diligence, including on-site client visits and conference calls, analysis of business models, assessment of management and servicing capabilities, and review of industry trends and applicable regulations.
- Identify structural strengths and weaknesses, evaluate downside scenarios, and recommend appropriate structural protections, covenants, triggers, reporting requirements, and other mitigants.
- Research and analyze financial and operating information relating to companies, counterparties, industries, and underlying asset pools.
- Assess the financial soundness of counterparties and underlying securitization assets, including leverage, liquidity, debt service capacity, historical performance, repayment capability, and sensitivity to stress.
- Perform financial statement analysis, including completion and review of spreading software (MRA), and reconcile analysis to source information.
- Review legal documentation for conformity with approved Credit terms and conditions and raise exceptions or execution risks promptly.
- Maintain current knowledge of securitization markets, relevant accounting and regulatory developments, Bank policies, and emerging credit risks.

Portfolio Management and Transaction Execution
- Assist Account Managers in managing assigned account and transaction responsibilities, including timely annual reviews, amendments, renewals, rating reviews, waivers, covenant monitoring, and internal trigger reporting.
- Serve as a secondary portfolio manager or day-to-day contact on assigned transactions and independently manage less complex transactions, subject to appropriate senior oversight.
- Continuously monitor transaction performance, collateral trends, counterparty financial performance, industry conditions, and emerging risks, and escalate material issues with a recommended course of action.
- Maintain complete and current financial, collateral, covenant, trigger, authorization, and exposure information for assigned clients and transactions.
- Provide clear analytical findings to Account Managers and Credit, including independent views on key risks, structural protections, and proposed mitigants.
- Prepare and deliver portfolio presentations, watchlist updates, ad hoc risk assessments, and materials for relevant business and Credit partners.
- Participate actively in client and internal discussions regarding transaction terms, credit issues, amendments, and ongoing portfolio matters.
- Apply detailed knowledge of Bank policies and standards to ensure the portfolio adheres to BMO policies and procedures, particularly those applicable to securitization products.
- Participate in the review and negotiation of legal documentation and coordinate resolution of open credit, legal, operational, and documentation items.
- Monitor exposure across BMO clients, products, legal entities, and facilities, and support escalation of concentration or limit matters.
- Coordinate AML/KYC processing and follow through on pending documentation and other closing or post-closing requirements.

Partnership, Leadership, and Business Support
- Liaise with Global Markets areas and with various lines of business, Credit, Legal, Capital, Finance, Compliance, and operational areas of the Bank as required.
- Partner with product and coverage teams on portfolio management needs, transaction execution, client opportunities, and growth initiatives.
- Participate as a core member of deal teams negotiating structure, credit terms, and documentation for securitization transactions.
- Contribute to updates of Financing Guidelines, underwriting standards, portfolio procedures, and related governance materials.
- Support projects involving regulatory, policy, data, reporting, process, or technology enhancements.
- Provide day-to-day guidance, quality review, and technical support to Analysts, and share knowledge across the team.
- Identify opportunities to improve the quality, consistency, efficiency, and control environment of underwriting and portfolio management processes.

Qualifications
- Undergraduate degree with strong academic achievement; coursework in finance, economics, accounting, mathematics, or a related discipline is preferred.
- Typically 3 to 6 years of relevant experience in credit, structured finance, securitization, corporate banking, capital markets, or a related analytical role. Equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered.
- Formal credit training and demonstrated experience preparing credit applications, conducting financial analysis, and assessing transaction structures are strongly preferred.
- Working knowledge of securitization or structured finance concepts, including collateral performance, cash flow waterfalls, credit enhancement, covenants, triggers, counterparty risk, and legal structure.
- Knowledge of capital markets and corporate and investment banking products, applicable regulations, and organizational lending and portfolio management policies.
- Advanced analytical capabilities across business, financial, credit, and transaction-structure analysis, with sound judgment and attention to material risk factors.
- Highly developed written and oral communication skills, including the ability to present complex analysis and recommendations clearly and concisely.
- Strong interpersonal skills and demonstrated effectiveness in a collaborative, fast-paced, and demanding team environment.
- Advanced proficiency in MS Excel and strong proficiency in MS Word and PowerPoint. Experience with Moody’s, Capital IQ, Bloomberg, cash flow modeling, and database management tools is preferred.
- Self-starter with strong attention to detail, effective prioritization skills, and the ability to manage multiple transactions and deadlines with limited supervision.
- Demonstrated ownership, initiative, and ability to anticipate next steps, identify issues early, and follow matters through to completion.
- Ability to support and develop junior team members through clear direction, constructive feedback, and knowledge sharing.

The salary range for this role is $115,000 up to $130,000 CAD (subject to the candidate meeting the specific skills, experience, education, and qualification requirements).

BMO Capital Markets is a leading, full-service financial services provider. We offer corporate and investment banking, treasury management, as well as research and advisory services to clients around the world. #bmocapitalmarkets

The Analyst will be part of the Global Markets Corporate Banking Securitization team, which is responsible for underwriting and account management of securitization and other structured finance transactions across a wide variety of asset classes, including (but not limited to) automobile loans and leases, equipment loans, student loans, credit cards, consumer installment loans, residential mortgage-backed securities, commercial mortgage-backed securities, and leveraged loans for U.S. and Canadian clients. The Analyst will support Account Management by providing due diligence and credit analysis on current and prospective clients and by making approval recommendations regarding deal structures and exposure amounts. The Analyst will also support a range of other portfolio management responsibilities.

Credit Risk and Financial Analyses
- Prepare concise, accurate and well-reasoned written credit applications and memoranda for both new and existing transactions for presentation to Credit.
- Conduct credit risk analysis of securitization transactions using all available sources of information including, but not limited to servicer reports, cash flow models, financial statements, servicer audits, legal documentation, etc.
- Determine estimated capital for current and prospective securitization transactions using the bank’s capital models.
- Conduct due diligence that includes on-site client visits and conference calls, analysis of business models, and comprehensive review of industry trends and related regulations.
- Analyze transactions for structural strengths and weaknesses and structure appropriately to mitigate weaknesses.
- Research and analyze financial and operating information relating to companies and industries.
- Assess financial soundness of counterparties and underlying securitization assets including appropriate debt levels, debt service, historic financial performance and repayment capabilities.
- Perform financial statement analysis including completion of spreading software (MRA).
- Review documentation for conformity with approved Credit terms and conditions.
- Keep abreast of industry trends and regulatory developments.

Portfolio Management Support
- Assist Account Managers in managing a diverse portfolio of accounts, including preparing concise credit reviews (as needed, at least annually) within required timeframes and continuously monitoring transaction performance and the financial performance of clients and their respective industries.
- Provide analytical findings to Account Management team including input on credit risks and related mitigants.
- Maintain current financial performance information on clients and securitization transactions in order to perform timely annual reviews, financial covenants, and internal trigger monitoring.
- Assist Account Managers in development of presentations or ad-hoc portfolio updates for relevant credit partners.
- Support Account Managers with portfolio management needs for the business.
- Participate in decision-making with clients and internal product group partners.
- Expert knowledge of Bank policies and standards to ensure portfolio adheres to BMO’s policies and procedures, especially as they pertain to the securitization product.
- Review and negotiation of legal documentation.
- Monitor exposure across different BMO clients and products.
- Assist in AML/KYC processing and obtain any pending required documentation.

- Liaise with Global Markets areas and with various lines of business and operational areas of the Bank as required.
- Support Global Markets areas on portfolio management needs and growth initiatives of the business.
- Participate in deal teams to negotiate structure and documentation for securitization transactions.
- Assist in updating Financing Guidelines.
- Participate in projects as required.

- An undergraduate degree with outstanding academic achievement.  Specific academic coursework in finance, economics, or accounting.
- 0–3 years of relevant experience (e.g., credit, structured finance, capital markets, or related analytical roles); formal credit training preferred.
- Analysts typically remain in this role for 1–3 years before advancing to the next level.
- Credit analysis experience and understanding are preferred; Global Markets–specific training will be provided.
- Knowledge of capital markets, investment banking products and applicable regulations.
- Knowledge of organizational lending and portfolio management policies and objectives.
- Excellent analytical skills to include business, financial, and credit analysis areas.
- Highly developed written and oral communication skills.
- Strong interpersonal skills used within a collaborative and demanding team environment.
- Expertise in financial computer applications and database management tools including MS Excel, Moody’s, Capital IQ and Bloomberg.
- Strong proficiency in other Microsoft Office products including MS Word and PowerPoint.
- Self-starter with keen attention to detail and ability to work under limited supervision.
- Ability to be creative, insightful, and resourceful in performance of duties.

- Excellent capability to independently function as part of a team through self-motivation.

Leads the implementation, oversight, maintenance, and continuous enhancement of enterprise-wide compliance programs and regulatory governance frameworks. jobs.title: Strategic Sourcing Manager
jobs.description:
Application Deadline:

10/16/2026

Address:
250 Yonge Street

Job Family Group:

Procurement

Job Summary

The Sourcing Manager, External Labor supports end-to-end sourcing for BMO's External Labor portfolio, including professional services, advisory services, technology services, staff augmentation, managed services, and project-based Statements of Work (SOWs). The role partners with business stakeholders to understand workforce needs, sourcing requirements, transformation priorities, and supplier strategies in order to deliver business value, manage risk, and optimize workforce-related spend.
This role acts as a trusted sourcing advisor to assigned business groups, helping stakeholders evaluate sourcing alternatives, supplier capabilities, commercial models, market conditions, and contract structures. The Sourcing Manager leads competitive sourcing events, supplier selection, due diligence, negotiation, contracting activities, and category initiatives while applying BMO's procurement, supplier risk, and governance requirements.
The successful candidate will bring strong sourcing fundamentals, analytical capability, stakeholder management skills, negotiation experience, and an interest in the evolving external workforce marketplace. Experience in professional services, contingent workforce, consulting, technology services, managed services, or SOW-based sourcing is strongly preferred.
Key Accountabilities

Category Strategy & End-to-End Sourcing Execution
- Lead end-to-end sourcing initiatives across the External Labor portfolio, including RFx events, supplier selection, due diligence, commercial evaluation, contract negotiation, renewal, and supplier onboarding.
- Develop and execute category and sub-category sourcing strategies that align stakeholder needs with market opportunities, enterprise priorities, and BMO business objectives.
- Support development of category management frameworks, sourcing roadmaps, project plans, supplier strategies, and recommendations for assigned External Labor spend areas.
- Conduct market and supply analysis to identify supplier capabilities, preferred suppliers, sourcing alternatives, market trends, and potential opportunities to improve cost, quality, speed, and risk outcomes.
- Apply disciplined sourcing methodologies, procurement policies, and project management practices to ensure sourcing initiatives are well controlled, well documented, and effectively executed.

External Labor Category Expertise
- Support sourcing activity across external labor sub-categories, including professional services, management consulting, advisory services, staff augmentation, technology services, managed services, and SOW-based engagements.
- Analyze labor market conditions, skill availability, geographic delivery models, supplier capabilities, rate benchmarks, and workforce trends to inform sourcing recommendations.
- Partner with stakeholders to understand external workforce needs, capacity constraints, specialized skill requirements, project demand, and transformation initiatives.
- Assist in evaluating supplier delivery models, including onshore, nearshore, offshore, staff augmentation, project-based, managed service, and outcome-oriented models.
- Maintain awareness of external labor market innovations, emerging workforce models, AI-enabled delivery capabilities, and supplier ecosystem trends that may impact category strategy.

Business Partnership & Advisory
- Act as a trusted advisor to assigned business stakeholders by understanding business priorities, workforce requirements, sourcing objectives, risk considerations, and stakeholder expectations.
- Influence stakeholder decision-making through data-driven insights, market intelligence, commercial analysis, and clear recommendations.
- Help stakeholders evaluate sourcing alternatives, supplier strategies, commercial structures, contract options, and supplier risk considerations.
- Build effective relationships with internal stakeholders, external suppliers, Legal, Compliance, Risk Support Areas, Third Party Risk teams, Finance, HR, and other enterprise partners.
- Communicate key messages, sourcing strategies, recommendations, risks, and results clearly and effectively across managerial levels.

Commercial Negotiation & Value Delivery
- Lead or support supplier negotiations to achieve competitive commercial outcomes while balancing cost, service quality, flexibility, delivery accountability, and risk management.
- Support development and negotiation of External Labor commercial models, including resource-based pricing, rate cards, supplier markups, time-and-materials arrangements, fixed-fee constructs, milestone-based SOW pricing, and other professional services pricing structures.
- Identify demand management, cost optimization, supplier consolidation, pricing improvement, and process efficiency opportunities across assigned categories and portfolios.
- Collaborate with suppliers and stakeholders to create value, improve performance, drive innovation, and support business outcomes.
- Develop business cases and sourcing recommendations that assess expected value, supplier options, commercial implications, risks, and implementation considerations.

Supplier Risk, Governance & Performance Management
- Performs initial supplier risk assessments and incorporates risk outcomes into sourcing recommendations, contracting strategies, and supplier governance plans.
- Partner with Legal, Regulatory Compliance, Risk Support Areas, Third Party Risk teams, and business stakeholders to ensure supplier engagements align with BMO policies, standards, and control expectations.
- Identify, quantify, and prioritize supplier-related risks, including operational risk, concentration risk, regulatory risk, contractual risk, performance risk, and delivery model risk.
- Support contract lifecycle activities, including creating, modifying, renewing, and terminating supplier agreements as required.
- Use supplier performance metrics, dashboards, reporting, and governance inputs to monitor supplier outcomes and identify opportunities for improvement.

Analytics, Insights & Continuous Improvement
- Conduct spend analysis, supplier analysis, market research, benchmark analysis, and contract analysis to inform sourcing strategies and business recommendations.
- Develop clear, actionable insights from data, research, stakeholder input, supplier information, and market intelligence.
- Maintain sourcing pipeline information, project status updates, reports, dashboards, and other materials that support effective planning and execution.
- Identify opportunities to enhance sourcing processes, improve stakeholder experience, increase speed-to-execution, and promote consistent use of category playbooks or sourcing templates.
- Stay current on procurement best practices, sourcing methodologies, external labor market trends, supplier models, regulatory considerations, and emerging technologies impacting external workforce sourcing.

Operating Model & Ways of Working

- Manage multiple sourcing projects simultaneously while resolving competing priorities and stakeholder objectives.
- Works independently and regularly handles non-routine situations with appropriate escalation and stakeholder engagement.
- Provides specialized sourcing, analytical, and technical support for assigned categories and stakeholder groups.
- Exercises judgment to identify, diagnose, and solve problems within established policies, standards, and risk requirements.
- Takes measured risks while protecting the bank by applying BMO's Risk Management Framework, making sound and risk-informed decisions aligned to business strategy, policy requirements, laws, and regulations.
- Broader work or accountabilities may be assigned as needed.

Who You Are

- You build trusted relationships across diverse stakeholder groups and collaborate effectively as One Bank.
- You communicate clearly in writing and conversation, including when explaining complex sourcing options, risks, or recommendations.
- You are curious, analytical, adaptable, and comfortable navigating ambiguity or incomplete information.
- You bring a commercial mindset and enjoy negotiating outcomes that balance value, flexibility, service quality, and risk.
- You take ownership, demonstrate initiative, and look for practical ways to improve processes, supplier outcomes, and stakeholder experience.
- You are organized, data-driven, and able to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic environment.

Qualifications - Required

- Typically 5 to 7 years of relevant strategic sourcing, procurement, category management, supply chain, consulting, or related experience, and a post-secondary degree in a related field of study or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
- Strong knowledge of sourcing and procurement processes, procedures, controls, and category management practices.
- Experience planning and executing competitive sourcing events, supplier evaluations, negotiations, and contract-related activities.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including ability to compile, synthesize, and draw insights from spend data, supplier information, market research, and stakeholder input.
- Demonstrated ability to assess risks, including identifying, quantifying, prioritizing, and incorporating risk considerations into sourcing recommendations.
- Strong negotiation, stakeholder management, collaboration, influence, verbal communication, and written communication skills.
- Ability to manage ambiguity, work independently, resolve conflicting priorities, and support multiple initiatives at the same time.
- Proficiency with Excel and spreadsheet analysis; comfort using data to support decisions and recommendations.

Qualifications - Preferred / Strongly Desired for External Labor

- Experience sourcing External Labor categories, including professional services, consulting, advisory services, staff augmentation, technology services, managed services, or SOW-based engagements.
- Experience negotiating Statements of Work, professional services agreements, staffing arrangements, managed services agreements, or other external workforce-related contracts.
- Familiarity with contingent workforce program models, VMS/MSP environments, supplier governance, and associated performance management practices.
- Experience supporting commercial model development or negotiation, including rate cards, supplier markups, time-and-materials pricing, fixed-fee SOWs, milestone-based pricing, or outcome-based constructs.
- Knowledge of labor market intelligence, skill availability trends, geographic rate variability, external workforce planning concepts, and supplier ecosystem dynamics.
- Experience in financial services, technology, consulting, or another highly regulated industry is an asset.
- Ability to prepare clear sourcing summaries, recommendation materials, risk considerations, and business cases for senior stakeholders.
