jobs.title: Manager, Community Partnership & Business Development
jobs.description:
Application Deadline:

10/30/2026

Address:
595 Burrard Street

Job Family Group:

Strategy & Change

Manager, Community Partnership & Business Development

The Customer Segments, Personal Banking team is responsible for defining, developing, and executing cross-functional, customer-centric strategies that drive Personal Banking customer acquisition, growth, and retention while supporting key business priorities.

As a key member of the New to Canada and Customer Growth team, the Manager, Community Partnerships & Business Development will be responsible for developing and executing community partnerships, sponsorships, events, and engagement strategies primarily focused on the South Asian market within the Greater Vancouver Area (GVA) .

The Manager, Community Partnerships & Business Development will play a key role in growing BMO’s market share and strengthening its presence within the South Asian community. This will be accomplished by building meaningful relationships with community organizations, business associations, Centres of Influence, cultural networks, community leaders, and other strategic partners.

Working closely with Regional Banking leadership, branch teams, Business Banking, Wealth Management, and corporate partners, the Manager, Community Partnerships & Business Development will identify and deliver opportunities that generate leads, increase customer acquisition, deepen client relationships, and promote BMO’s broader value proposition.

The successful candidate will build specialized knowledge of the South Asian market and become a subject matter expert in community engagement, partnership development, lead generation, and customer acquisition. The ability to translate community relationships and market opportunities into measurable business results will be key to success in this role.

A typical workday may include:
- Working closely with Personal and Business Banking Regional Leaders to develop and execute a community engagement, sponsorship, and partnership plan aligned with regional customer growth priorities.
- Developing and executing strategies to grow BMO’s market share and strengthen its presence within the South Asian community, with a particular focus on the Greater Vancouver Area.
- Identifying, developing, and maintaining relationships with community leaders, business associations, cultural organizations, non-profit organizations, educational institutions, referral partners, and Centres of Influence.
- Leading BMO’s involvement in large-scale South Asian community events and sponsorships, as well as select additional events and partnership opportunities where appropriate.
- Identifying sponsorships, partnerships, and community initiatives that enhance BMO’s visibility, reputation, and relevance within the South Asian market.
- Establishing proactive community outreach to increase awareness of BMO’s products, services, customer offers, and New to Canada solutions.
- Representing BMO at key community, cultural, business, sponsorship, and networking events throughout the Greater Vancouver Area.
- Creating speaking, networking, and relationship-building opportunities that promote BMO’s broader value proposition and deepen client and community relationships.
- Developing and maintaining a strategic engagement plan for key community leaders, organizations, and referral partners.
- Consulting with community partners, Centres of Influence, and Regional Personal and Business Banking Leaders to identify and execute market development opportunities.
- Supporting branch teams in preparing for and participating in community events, partnership meetings, presentations, and business development opportunities.
- Collaborating with branch leaders and frontline teams to generate leads, facilitate referrals, and convert opportunities into new customer relationships.
- Partnering closely with Business Banking and Wealth Management teams to identify and facilitate referrals, bring partners into appropriate community events, and present BMO’s broader capabilities to prospective and existing clients.
- Collaborating with New to Canada Market Ambassadors and branch teams to build community engagement and customer acquisition capabilities.
- Supporting international student and campus partnership initiatives within British Columbia, with a focus on the Greater Vancouver Area, and communicating results to key stakeholders.
- Providing coaching and guidance to branch teams on community engagement, customer acquisition, lead management, partnership development, and relationship-building best practices.
- Monitoring and reporting on customer acquisition, lead generation, branch referrals, products per customer, balances, and other relevant business outcomes.
- Tracking weekly, monthly, and quarterly activities and outcomes, including community engagements, partnership development, branch referrals, leads, new customer acquisitions, Personal and Premium Client opportunities, and cross-sell opportunities.
- Gathering and sharing feedback from the field to enhance customer value propositions, community strategies, and customer acquisition approaches, with customer needs, competitive activity, market potential, and profitability in mind.
- Sharing market intelligence regarding emerging South Asian community trends, customer needs, competitor activity, and potential business development opportunities.
- Supporting the continued innovation and evolution of Personal Banking products, services, customer offers, and community engagement strategies.
- Acting as a key liaison between regional stakeholders and corporate partners to ensure alignment with Customer Growth, New to Canada, and broader strategic priorities.

Knowledge, Skills, and Qualifications
- A bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education and relevant business experience.
- At least seven years of relevant experience in business development, partnership management, community engagement, customer acquisition, sales leadership, or a related field.
- Demonstrated experience working with South Asian communities, organizations, business associations, cultural networks, or community leaders within the Greater Vancouver Area is strongly preferred.
- Strong knowledge of the South Asian community and business landscape within the Greater Vancouver Area.
- Demonstrated ability to develop trusted relationships within diverse communities and cultural networks.
- Proven track record of developing, negotiating, and managing partnerships that deliver measurable customer and business outcomes.
- Experience planning and executing community events, sponsorship activations, outreach programs, or market development initiatives.
- Strong understanding of customer acquisition, lead generation, referral management, and relationship-deepening strategies.
- Ability to influence, collaborate with, and lead diverse and cross-functional stakeholder groups.
- Strong relationship-building, networking, consulting, and stakeholder-management capabilities.
- Solid leadership skills and the ability to provide coaching and guidance to branch teams and business partners.
- Excellent verbal and written communication, facilitation, and presentation skills.
- Strong active listening and coaching skills.
- Comfort interpreting customer, segment, and market data to identify trends, opportunities, and business insights.
- Experience tracking activities, measuring outcomes, and communicating results to senior stakeholders.
- Resilience and adaptability in the face of ambiguity, evolving priorities, or setbacks.
- Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and remain organized in a dynamic environment.
- Advanced Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint skills.
- Strong social selling and professional networking capabilities.
- The role is based in the Greater Vancouver Area, with regular in-person engagement across the market.
- Five days per week in the office or market and approximately 40% local travel required. Mileage is compensated in accordance with applicable policies.

Key Performance Measures
The primary measure of success for this role will be core customer acquisition.

Performance will also be assessed through activity and outcome tracking, including:
- Growth in BMO’s presence and market share within the South Asian community.
- New customer acquisitions.
- Qualified lead generation.
- Branch referral generation and conversion.
- Personal and Premium Client opportunities.
- Business Banking and Wealth Management referrals.
- Cross-sell and relationship-deepening opportunities.
- Community partnership and stakeholder development.
- Effectiveness of sponsorships, events, and community activations.
- Weekly, monthly, and quarterly activity and outcome reporting.
- Contribution to regional Customer Growth and New to Canada priorities.

Key Relationships
Working closely with:
- Regional Banking Leadership.
- Branch Leaders and frontline teams.
- Business Banking partners.
- Wealth Management partners.
- Customer Segments and Customer Growth teams.
- New to Canada partners and Market Ambassadors.
- South Asian community organizations and business associations.
- Centres of Influence and referral partners.
- Cultural and non-profit organizations.
- Educational institutions.
- Sponsorship and event partners.
- Community, cultural, and business leaders.

This role offers a unique opportunity to directly influence BMO’s growth within the South Asian market by building meaningful community relationships, executing high-impact partnerships and events, generating new business opportunities, and strengthening BMO’s presence throughout the Greater Vancouver Area.

jobs.description:
Application Deadline:

Address:
100 King Street West

Job Family Group:

Audit, Risk & Compliance

Oversees, monitors, and reports on information and technology risks for a designated portfolio. Develops and monitors the risk management and governance framework and practices leveraged across BMO to manage information and technology risks. Develops and monitors adherence to policies, standards, methodologies, and controls that increase transparency, accuracy, and consistency across groups. Works with stakeholders to implement the methodology, metrics, and program standards for the assigned portfolio to ensure compliance, effective monitoring, timely reporting, and identify action plans.

Key Accountabilities:
·   Administers and maintains technology and information security and management risk program activities, adhering to applicable policies, procedures, and established processes.
·   Reviews new business initiatives and monitors existing initiatives to identify potential risk situations and impacts; makes recommendations or escalates in accordance with established guidelines.
·   Identifies potential risk situations and impacts and makes recommendations or escalates, as appropriate.
·   Provides advice and guidance to assigned business or groups on implementation of the risk framework, including effective challenge.
·   Coordinates and participates in the execution of oversight and governance activities, including reporting; assessment of education and training needs; development and delivery of training; and development and execution of regulatory administration processes and procedures.
·   Consults with stakeholders to improve the consistency and transparency of risk measurement, metrics, and reporting.
·   Supports the development and maintenance of the governance system and framework, including policy, standard, and operating procedure lifecycle management, as well as education and training assessments.
·   Builds effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including business stakeholders and corporate support areas, to provide second line of defense information and technology risk management support.
·   Manages databases and supports analysis, forecasting, and data visualization, ensuring adherence to data governance standards.
·   Analyzes data and information to provide insights and recommendations, including identifying risk impacts associated with new processes and workflows related to initiatives.
·   Maintains tools and templates for information and technology risk programs and standards, including Risk Control Self Assessment (RCSA), Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX), business continuity planning standards, and policies for internal and third-party solution development.
·   Develops and maintains in-depth knowledge of business and related risk management requirements and legislative and regulatory directives and guidance.
·   Builds effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
·   Analyzes data and information to provide insights and recommendations.
Cloud Technology Governance:
·   Assesses and monitors risks associated with cloud technologies, including concentration risk, third-party dependencies, cloud-native services, container platforms, and emerging cloud architectures.
·   Reviews cloud governance controls and risk management practices to ensure alignment with enterprise standards, regulatory expectations, and risk appetite.
·   Supports the development and enhancement of cloud-related risk metrics, key risk indicators (KRIs), reporting, and governance processes.
·   Engages with technology stakeholders to evaluate cloud adoption initiatives and identify potential risk impacts related to security, availability, recoverability, data management, and operational resilience.
Artificial Intelligence Risk and Governance:

- In-depth knowledge of online investing brokerage platforms, pricing, and operational processes.
- Strong commercial and business acumen.
- Strong relationship management, stakeholder engagement, and partnership-building capabilities.
- Training, coaching, and facilitation experience preferred.
- Demonstrated ability to move with pace, manage competing priorities, and lead through change.
- Demonstrated commitment to continuous improvement and strengthening business performance.

jobs.description:

Advanced Analytical & Technical Expertise
- Applies expert‑level analytical skills to break down complex credit risk problems, integrating data from multiple internal and external sources to produce insights, recommendations, and decision‑ready materials.
- Designs and produces sophisticated recurring and ad‑hoc reports, dashboards, and analytical tools to support credit risk monitoring and regulatory expectations.
- Conducts advanced credit portfolio analytics including vintage analysis, trend assessments, risk segmentation, and predictive analysis to identify emerging risks and portfolio vulnerabilities.
- Supports the development of risk decision strategies including data analytics, simulation, validation testing, and reporting requirements to evaluate the effectiveness of new or modified strategies.

Data Management & Reporting Leadership
- Defines business requirements for analytics and reporting to ensure data insights inform senior‑level decisions and align with enterprise standards.
- Ensures strong governance and effective controls for data quality, lineage, and use of key risk indicators (KRIs), including the development, calibration, and ongoing monitoring of KRIs for Business Banking.
- Participates in and may lead components of strategic initiatives related to credit risk analytics, reporting transformation, and process modernization.

Subject‑Matter Expertise & Consultation
- Acts as a subject matter expert on regulatory, policy, and industry requirements related to credit risk, risk reporting, and analytics.
- Provides strategic input to senior leaders regarding portfolio quality, emerging risks, model or policy impacts, and opportunities to enhance monitoring capabilities.
- Serves as a key partner to first‑ and second‑line stakeholders, offering effective challenge and analytical guidance on business banking originations, credit policy changes, and portfolio strategies.

Programming & Tools
- Advanced proficiency in SAS, Python, and Power BI, with the ability to automate processes, build analytical models, integrate multiple data sources, and design interactive dashboards.
- Ability to perform complex portfolio analytics, including vintage curves, cohort performance tracking, segmentation modeling, and early‑warning indicator development.

Risk Management Expertise
- In‑depth knowledge of credit risk management theory, risk systems, reporting frameworks, and Business Banking lending products.
- Demonstrated experience with KRIs, KPIs, capital‑at‑risk assessments, and other advanced credit portfolio metrics.
- Strong understanding of regulatory expectations and internal policies impacting reporting and portfolio oversight.

Communication & Influence
- Skilled in conveying complex analytical findings to senior stakeholders through clear narratives, visualizations, and recommendations.
- Proven ability to influence decision‑making in ambiguous or data‑limited environments, supporting cross‑functional alignment.

Ideal Candidate Profile
- A seasoned analytical professional with 7+ years of experience in credit risk analytics, preferably within Business Banking or mid‑market lending.
- Deep technical fluency in statistical analysis, programming, and risk reporting systems.
- Demonstrated ability to independently own complex analysis and produce insights that shape policy, risk appetite, and portfolio strategy.

Director - Financial Services Group

Global Team Overview:
The selected candidate will join the Financial Services Group (FSG), part of Advisory Solutions within BMO Commercial Bank, Canada. The Group focuses on management and origination of banking relationships within the Financial Services sector, with a focus on senior debt financing opportunities with non-regulated lenders or long-term lessors as well as full banking relationships with specific financial services sub-sectors.  The team assesses financing opportunities representing $10MM or more, both on a syndicated and bilateral basis, for both private and public companies in Canada. The Group is based in Toronto and has national coverage in the sector.

Job Overview
The Director will join the FSG team that is responsible for senior secured loan origination and account management of a growing portfolio of clients. The Director will have direct portfolio management responsibilities of an existing portfolio comprised of lending relationships with complex credit structures and important cash management needs. This includes making credit approval recommendations and working collaboratively with various Corporate Finance representatives to best serve and manage these existing client relationships as well as grow the portfolio by adding new relationships.

- Manages the risk of the assigned complex portfolio in a timely and precise manner.

- Acts as daily sales contact for clients on sales related questions such as product information, pricing, implementation timeframes and requirements.

- Directly manages the annual review process, interim reviews, specified quarterly reports and resolution of exceptions.

- Assists team in pre-sales activities such as pitch preparation, client research, preparation of prospect and client files for further action.

- Assists with sales and service administration and processing to ensure client experience is seamless and opportunities are identified and met.

- Gathers data to advance sale process and completes all required documentation.

- Manages transaction requests to keep the process on track with timelines.

- Tracks internal reports and recommends improvements to sales support materials based on findings and feedback.

- Maintains accurate documentation and ensure adherence to prescribed policies and procedures and overall safety of the Bank’s position.

- Maintains current client information on Bank system/files to ensure client history is accurate and complete.

- Applies expertise and thinks creatively to address unique or ambiguous situations and to find solutions to problems that can be complex and non-routine.

- Broader work or accountabilities may be assigned as needed.

- Credit Qualifications and associated credit knowledge and skills according to the established qualification standards

- Demonstrated knowledge of relevant industry verticals and market’s competitive environment

- Experience in contract negotiations with both clients and legal counsel

jobs.title: Vice President, Corporate Banking- Corporate Banking Risk Management & Initiatives
jobs.description:
Application Deadline:

10/30/2026

Address:
100 King Street West

Job Family Group:

Capital Mrkts Sales & Service

The salary range for this role is $125,000 up to $135,000 CAD (subject to the candidate meeting the specific skills, experience, education, and qualification requirements)

Job Description
The Vice President will support Corporate Banking professionals in executing the first line of defense accountability for strong risk culture. The role provides coordination, analysis, reporting, and oversight support across regulatory initiatives, risk assessments, policy governance, remediation programs, committee governance, and data quality initiatives.

KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY
Key Area Weight
Regulatory Exam and Internal Audit Coordination: 30%
Projects and Initiatives: 40%
Analytics: 30%

ACCOUNTABILITIES DEFINED
A.  Regulatory Change, Remediation and Internal Audit Coordination
- Lead organization and gathering of “first day” materials for audit, credit risk review and regulatory exams
- Participate in regulatory and internal audit/credit risk review meetings
- Coordinate business responses to regulatory consultations, reviews, examinations, and information requests.
- Support implementation and tracking of regulatory remediation programs.
- Assist in annual and ad hoc risk identification and risk assessment exercises.
- Consolidate stakeholder feedback and prepare management summaries and recommendations.
- Coordinate policy, standard, and guideline reviews across relevant stakeholders.
- Maintain inventories of policy governance, regulatory commitments, and risk assessments.
- Track approvals, attestations, action items, and implementation milestones.

B.  Projects/Initiatives
- Act as Global Corporate Banking representative on risk and regulatory related projects as the credit environment and economic events dictate
- Interact with Wholesale Credit Methodology on matters regarding Credit Risk Measures as needed.
- Interact with Operational Risk team on data quality reviews or other initiatives impacting the Corporate Bank
- Facilitate consistent implementation of mandates across the Global Corporate Bank and lead certain training initiatives
- Advocate for the Corporate Bank on enterprise-wide initiatives
- Review and assess proposed changes/updates to Corporate Policies, Standards and Operating Procedures for continued suitability for Corporate Bank. Strive to be Subject Matter Expert on these topics
- Respond to banker Inquiries on varying credit risk policies/procedural topics

C.  Analytics
- Evaluate eligibility of credit facilities for inclusion in risk transfer portfolios on as needed basis.
- Analyze portfolio data to identify underlying drivers of changing metrics.
- Assess impact of emerging risk events as the environment dictates
- Support data quality reviews, issue tracking, and capability-building initiatives.
- Assist in developing and delivering risk-related communications and training materials.
- Respond to business inquiries regarding governance processes, policies, and regulatory requirements.
- Support ad hoc analysis and executive briefing materials for senior management.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS
This role requires the incumbent to interact with the following processes and/or groups:
- Corporate Banking/GM Corporate Banking personnel at all levels
- Enterprise Risk (Risk Reporting, Wholesale Credit, Portfolio Management, WCM)
- Other Operating Groups (US and Canadian Commercial)
- Corporate Audit and Credit Risk Review teams
- Business Intelligence & Analytics
- Risk and Capital Solutions

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS
Knowledge:
- Undergraduate degree in finance, business, economics, accounting, risk management, or a related discipline.
- 3-7 years of banking, risk management, governance, credit, audit, regulatory, compliance, project management, or related experience.
- Knowledge of Commercial Banking and lending processes.
- Understanding of risk governance, policy management, regulatory expectations, and control frameworks.
- Familiarity with audit, issue management, remediation, and governance processes.
- Working knowledge of credit risk concepts and portfolio management practices considered an asset.

Skills:
- Reasoning and problem-solving skills
- Superior written and oral communication
- Exceptional quantitative analytics and credit analysis skills
- Strong interpersonal skills used within a team environment
- Strong ability to advocate persuasively
- Strong attention to detail
- Ability to work independently and to learn and adapt quickly.
- Ability to be creative, insightful, and resourceful in performance of duties

Delivers exceptional service to BMO customers and prospects. Identifies customer needs and provides advice and guidance regarding financial solutions that are in the best interests of customers. - Collaborates with BMO partners to identify referral opportunities that further grow the customer’s relationship with BMO beyond personal banking.
- Welcomes and guides customers as they walk into the branch lobby, and offers advice and guidance on available digital and self-serve options with the goal of making it easy, simple, and fast to bank with BMO.

- Meets customer transaction-based needs with seamless execution.
- Reviews customer profiles and engages customers in a needs-based conversation to identify potential opportunities and address everyday banking plans and credit card needs.
- Contributes to meeting branch business results and the customer experience.
- Supports operational activities (e.g. inventory management, escalated service requests, following up on customer applications, filing, opening and closing activities).
- Acts as a key member of a collaborative and versatile branch and market team.
- Probes to understand customer personal banking and credit card needs and integrates marketing promotions and programs into customer conversations to provide strategic advice.
- Organizes work information to ensure accuracy and completeness.
- Takes the initiative to find creative approaches that make each customer’s experience feel personal.
- Looks for ways to contribute to the ongoing improvement of the overall customer experience.
- Contributes to business results and the overall experience delivered.
- May work at multiple branches or through various channels based on market needs; work schedule may differ from week to week in terms of days worked, hours, and shifts.
- Follows through on risk and compliance processes and policies to ensure we safeguard our customers’ assets, maintain their privacy, and act in their best interest.
- Keeps current with the wider financial services marketplace, the legal and regulatory environment, and our commitment to uphold the highest ethical requirements of our industry.
- Maintains current knowledge of personal banking products, practices, and trends and integrates into customer conversations.
- Identifies and reports suspicious patterns of activity that are suspected to be related to money laundering.
- Complies with legal and regulatory requirements for the jurisdiction.

- Completes complex & diverse tasks within given rules/limits.
- Analyzes issues and determines next steps; escalates as required.

- Drive to deliver a personal customer experience.

- Resourceful self-starter with courage and confidence to approach customers.
- Readiness to collaborate and work in different capacities as part of a team.
- Strong interpersonal skills, including the ability to build rapport and connections with customers.
- An aptitude for listening, solving problems, and responding flexibly and creatively to new challenges.

- Verbal & written communication skills - Good.

- Analytical and problem solving skills - Good.

jobs.description:
Application Deadline:

10/18/2026

Address:
51 rue Notre-Dame est

Job Family Group:

Retail Banking Sales & Service

Description d'emploi

Offrir un service exceptionnel aux clients actuels et potentiels de BMO. Déterminer les besoins des clients et fournir des avis et des conseils quant aux solutions financières qui sont dans l’intérêt supérieur du client. Travailler en collaboration avec les partenaires de BMO au sein de la succursale et par l’intermédiaire de différents circuits, de manière à offrir l’expérience client souhaitée et à atteindre les objectifs d’ensemble.

- Collaborer avec les partenaires de BMO pour cerner les occasions d’indications de clients permettant d’élargir la relation des clients avec l’organisation au-delà des services bancaires aux particuliers.

- Accueillir chaleureusement les clients et les guider dès leur entrée dans la succursale en les conseillant et en les orientant quant aux options numériques et de libre-service offertes, pour que leurs transactions bancaires à BMO soient conviviales, faciles et rapides.

- À titre de responsable de l’accueil, participer à la réalisation des entretiens clients sur les services bancaires afin de recommander des circuits de distribution complémentaires et de fournir des conseils en matière de services bancaires aux particuliers et de placements.

- Répondre aux besoins des clients en matière de transactions bancaires sans difficulté.

- Passer en revue les profils des clients et amorcer avec eux un entretien axé sur leurs besoins afin de repérer de possibles occasions de lui offrir des programmes de services bancaires courants et un choix de cartes de crédit.

- Contribuer à l’atteinte des résultats de la succursale et à l’expérience client.

- Collaborer aux activités opérationnelles (p. ex., la gestion des stocks, la transmission à l’échelon supérieur des demandes de service, le suivi des demandes de clients, le classement et les activités d’ouverture et de fermeture).

- Agir à titre de membre clé d’une équipe collaborative et polyvalente en succursale et locale.

- Chercher à comprendre les besoins des clients en matière de services bancaires aux particuliers et de cartes de crédit et intégrer des offres promotionnelles et des programmes de marketing aux entretiens avec les clients afin de leur donner des conseils stratégiques.

- Classer les renseignements pour assurer l’exactitude et l’exhaustivité.

- Prendre l’initiative d’appliquer des approches créatives pour conférer une dimension humaine à chaque expérience client.

- Chercher des façons de prendre part à l’amélioration continue de l’expérience client globale.

- Contribuer aux résultats d’affaires ainsi qu’à l’expérience globale offerte.

- Au besoin, remplir ses fonctions dans plusieurs succursales et par l’intermédiaire de différents circuits selon les besoins du marché; l’horaire de travail peut varier d’une semaine à l’autre, en fait de jours, d’heures et de quarts.

- Assurer le suivi des politiques et des processus en matière de risque et de conformité pour veiller à protéger les actifs de nos clients ainsi que leur confidentialité et à agir dans leur intérêt.

- Demeurer au fait de ce qui se passe dans l’ensemble du marché des services financiers, de la législation et de la réglementation, ainsi que de notre engagement à respecter les exigences éthiques les plus rigoureuses du secteur.

- Tenir à jour ses connaissances liées aux produits, aux pratiques et aux tendances des services bancaires aux particuliers, et intégrer celles-ci dans les entretiens avec les clients.

- Déceler et signaler toute habitude suspecte pouvant être associée au blanchiment d’argent.

- Respecter les exigences juridiques et réglementaires du territoire.

- Protéger les actifs de la Banque conformément à toutes les exigences juridiques, réglementaires et éthiques.

- Exécuter des tâches complexes et diversifiées en respectant les règles et les limites établies.

- Analyser les problèmes et déterminer les prochaines étapes; transmettre à l’échelon supérieur au besoin.

- Des tâches et des responsabilités plus larges peuvent être attribuées au besoin.

- Prendre des risques mesurés tout en protégeant la Banque en appliquant notre cadre de gestion des risques dans l’exécution de vos fonctions, conformément à notre culture de gestion des risques et à notre appétit pour le risque approuvé, en prenant des décisions éclairées fondées sur le risque qui s’harmonisent à la stratégie d’affaires, protègent les actifs et respectent les documents de politique applicables (cadres, politiques, normes, procédures et documents connexes), les lois et la réglementation.

Qualifications :
- Généralement d’une à deux années d’expérience professionnelle pertinente et/ou certification dans un domaine connexe souhaitable, ou combinaison équivalente de scolarité et d’expérience.

- Canada seulement : Titre donnant droit à la vente de produits de placement, déjà obtenu ou en voie d’obtention (délai maximal de douze mois) – conformément aux exigences du territoire.

- Aisance et expérience dans l’utilisation des médias sociaux, des tablettes, des téléphones intelligents, des outils en ligne et des applications.

- Expérience en vente ou en service à la clientèle à caractère consultatif, associée à une grande motivation à offrir une expérience client personnelle.

- Connaissances de base des ventes spécialisées et des solutions de services bancaires aux entreprises pour diriger les clients vers des spécialistes.

- Engagement passionné à aider les clients.

- Grande motivation à offrir une expérience client personnalisée.

- Intérêt marqué pour les résultats et capacité à réussir dans un environnement de vente consultative et de travail en équipe.

- Personnalité ingénieuse et entreprenante en mesure d’approcher les clients avec confiance et courage.

- Promptitude à collaborer et à effectuer différentes tâches au sein d’une équipe.

- Solides aptitudes en relations interpersonnelles, y compris celle d’établir une relation et de créer des liens avec les clients.

- Aptitude à être à l’écoute, à résoudre des problèmes et à réagir de manière souple et créatrice aux nouveaux défis.

- Connaissances spécialisées – compétences de base.

- Compétences en communication orale et écrite – bonnes compétences.

- Compétences en organisation – bonnes compétences.

- Compétences pour la collaboration et le travail d’équipe – bonnes compétences.

- Compétences en analyse et en résolution de problèmes – bonnes compétences.
